articles.title: Every LEGO Book Nook and Bookend Set Available to Buy in 2026
articles.summary: Hide some LEGO within your book collection.
articles.body:
LEGO hasn't been just for kids for a while now. There are countless "adults welcome" LEGO sets that are perfect for offices, game rooms, or to mount on your walls. Sure, most of these sets are nerd-adjacent, from Star Wars display models to an enormous Lord of the Rings Rivendell set, but they are a testament to just how much the toy brand has changed over the years. Some of the biggest upcoming LEGO sets are 18+ builds specifically targeted at adult collectors this year. And If you're both an avid reader and huge LEGO fan like me, the three new themed book nooks now available are absolutely worth checking out. These book nooks are an entirely new type of LEGO set made to fit perfectly on your shelf and live amongst your book collection. If you're on the hunt for a perfect gift for the reader in your life, look no further.

With this new type of set available now, LEGO joins a wide range of brands offering book nook kits for adults in 2026. Below we've featured all of the options currently available, including a couple of pairs of bookends as well.

Every LEGO Book Nook and Bookend Available Now

The first three LEGO book nooks came out last year alongside the rest of the June 2025 LEGO lineup . Since then, LEGO has added several sets that act as the perfect book accessory for your collection. They're all riddled with detail and Easter eggs from their respective series and are modular; there's the folded in book nook style and the "unfolded" view. The unfolded mode offers a great display of famous scenes like the Harry and Ron finding Platform 9 3/4 or Gandalf facing off against the Balrog. The modularity makes these sets not only serve their purpose as book nooks well but also as standalone LEGO display pieces for your shelves or coffee tables.

The two separate sets of bookends function a little bit differently by replacing the idea of a simple nook with more of a functional aspect. This is the only bookends set we've seen so far.

We built the Lord of the Rings LEGO Book Nook and found it to be delightful. It includes a super detailed Gandalf minifigure with his sword and staff and a buildable, fully posable Balrog figure. It recreates the iconic scene on the Bridge of Khazad-dûm in the Fellowship of the Ring, with a plaque stating "you shall not pass!" front and center. It's 1,201 pieces and is sure to be a fun build, especially if you have the movie playing in the background!

As a book nook, this set would also go great alongside a collection of Lord of the Rings books or LotR Blu-rays . Since it's release it has also topped our list of the best Lord of the Rings gifts for fans of the series alongside a similarly cool set of non-lego bookends .

The LEGO Sherlock Holmes Book Nook is the biggest of the trio, coming it at 1,359 pieces, and definitely has the most Easter eggs — fitting for our favorite detective. When folded in nook form, the outer cover has the iconic silhouette of Sherlock and his magnifying glass from the actual Arthur Conan Doyle books . This set also comes with five detailed minifigures: Sherlock, Dr. Watson, Moriarty, Irene Adler, and seemingly a member of the Baker Street Irregulars. When unfolded, it's a detailed recreation of 221B Baker Street in London where Sherlock lives. You can check out the video below to get a closer look.

The LEGO Harry Potter Hogwarts Express Book Nook should be familiar to longtime LEGO fans, since the iconic red train has seen many iterations over the years . Of the three, I'd prefer to have this unfolded as it seemlessly splits the scene between King's Cross station in London and the magical Platfrom 9 3/4. It looks a bit silly folded in book nook mode in my opinion, but it still works. At 832 pieces, it's the smallest of the three, but included are Harry Potter and Ron Weasley minifigures along with their trolleys, Hedwig, and Scabbers. If you're looking for a set of bookends for your Harry Potter book collection , this is a great gift idea for any Harry Potter fan .

We had the chance to build the LEGO Wicked bookends and found them to be a great alternative to the more traditional book nooks. This is essentially two sets in one and you build both bookends separately before placing them on your shelf. The insdie of each book houses a little scene that allow them to double as a book nook if you turn them on their side.

Although we haven't gotten any updates about any new book nooks this year, LEGO did just release some new bookends. The Toy Story Slinky Dog Bookends are the first ever adult build in the Toy Story theme and features two adorable minifigures. I actually had the chance to build these bookends and loved being able to put together one of my favorite characters from my childhood in such a format. You can check out my build experience below.

We Build LEGO Toy Story Slinky Dog Bookends

The Dumbledore's office book nook was first released in June 2026 . It's a follow up to the Hogwarts Express set, making it the second Harry Potter book nook. At 1,182 pieces it's got a ton of little details you'd expect to see from within the greatest wizard's office. It also comes with Harry Potter and Dumbledore minifigures as well as two different versions of Fawkes.

Although the original set isn't a book nook, there is a popular alternate version of the LEGO Medieval Horse Knight Castle circulating the internet that is worth checking out. The Horse Knight Castle is already a 3-in-1 set, and the book nook version is just another way of building it. The original design from user The_Astral_J can be found on Rebrickable for $8. You will need to buy the set separately, which costs $129.99.

As of September 2026, there is only one upcoming LEGO Book Nook of note and its a full-on bookstore. The LEGO Icons Bookstore: Book Nook is set to release on October 1 for $149.99 and isn't connected to any major franchises. The success of the initial book nooks last year would indicate that LEGO will almost certainly be releasing more in the near future. We can only speculate as to which franchises will get the book nook treatment next, but since LEGO hasn't strayed beyond collaborations that are directly tied to book series', there's only so many potential next steps.

The first and most obvious next book nook would be an expansion of Dune. There has only been one LEGO Dune set so far and it was overall very popular thaks to the new movies and fans of the original book series . Something like a giant sand worm book nook would be a great choice. It's possible Disney could also join the fray with a Winnie the Pooh set or something similar. There are already a ton of LEGO Disney sets and this seems like a prime opportunity to put out a really interest Disney gift set for readers.

Myles Obenza is a freelance writer for IGN. Follow him on Bluesky @mylesobenza.bsky.social .

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney Criticized by Female Athletes as Nude Sports Trading App Ad Sparks Backlash
articles.summary: Euphoria star Sydney Sweeney has sparked yet another backlash for an advert after appearing nude in a series of promotional videos for sports trading app Novig.
articles.body:
Euphoria star Sydney Sweeney has sparked yet another backlash for an advert after appearing nude in a series of promotional videos for sports trading app Novig.

In the ads, the Madame Web star appears mostly naked, covered only by footballs, basketballs, and other sports paraphernalia. “Novig is just sports,” Sweeney says. “So they wanted to show just sports.”

The visual gags, pointing to Novig’s mission statement of being a trading app focused solely on sports (eschewing unrelated topics found on competing prediction markets), have sparked no end of controversy — both about Sweeney’s lack of clothing and how its imagery reflects on female athletes.

Confirmed: Sydney Sweeney knows ball. pic.twitter.com/EXQ4PzVZsi — Novig (@Novig) September 9, 2026

Confirmed: Sydney Sweeney knows ball. pic.twitter.com/EXQ4PzVZsi

Several high-profile women in sports have spoken out against Novig’s advertisements, with Australian professional boxer Skye Nicolson writing on Instagram, “Companies doing these ad campaigns should DO BETTER.”

“It’s the disrespect on athletes who dedicate their life to sport and to the women who have broken barriers for generations, to then have it made a mockery of by using a sex symbol using suggestive language and imagery in an ad about sport,” she added in a now-deleted Instagram story.

Gracie Kramer, a former UCLA gymnast who’s been one of the most outspoken female athletes regarding this situation, also chimed in. “I don’t know what Sydney Sweeney was doing, but this is what a woman in sports looks like,” she wrote on Instagram, along with footage from her competitions.

Tilly Kearns, a two-time Olympic water polo athlete, also posted a viral reel to Instagram, captioned, “I absolutely f**king hate Sydney Sweeney’s new sports ad.” The video showed several clips from her water polo meets, training sessions, and medalling ceremonies.

“Like, what are we doing … so much worse than I imagined, too. Here’s some real women sports content,” she wrote.

Speaking to the BBC , British sprinter Amy Hunt called out the campaign after running the 200-meter dash at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest, telling the outlet’s camera crews, “Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like.”

These are just a few of the many statements to have emerged from high-profile athletes in the aftermath of Sweeney’s Novig ads, and they haven’t gone without notice. Sweeney reportedly responded to the backlash on her Instagram stories, sharing a handful of covers from ESPN’s Body Issue, which notably feature images of nude athletes.

Speaking to Complex , Sweeney said called the ad campaign “a very simple and playful idea. She insisted "I grew up loving sports," adding: "I played sports growing up. I was on a soccer team, I was on a softball team, I was on a snow ski team. I learned how to slalom ski when I was little, and I did MMA. So sports have been a really big part of my life, and I love watching hockey and boxing, especially after playing Christie Martin. I have a really huge appreciation for every single fighter.”

The outrage has gotten so bad that Sweeney's social media presence is suffering; as noted by Variety , her account has lost over 200,000 followers amid the backlash. It's worth noting though that the Hollywood star still has 25.7 million followers on Instagram.

This isn’t the first time an advertisement featuring Sydney Sweeney has come under fire. You might remember the outrage that resulted from her 2025 campaign with American Eagle, which sparked debate over the play on words regarding “jeans” and “genes,” prompting accusations of racism against both Sweeney and the clothing brand, though American Eagle clarified that its ad was merely meant to highlight the fact that "great jeans look good on everyone."

Sweeney is clearly leaning into her status as a sex symbol, with her Novig ad campaign being the latest example of this. Back in May 2025, she turned heads for selling her own bathwater in a partnership with Dr. Squatch, a body wash and soap brand, which also sparked debate among fans and critics.

In terms of upcoming acting projects, Sweeney is down to appear in The Housemaid's Secret and the live-action Gundam movie. In July, it was reported that Sweeney had signed a deal to star in a new Sleepy Hollow movie . Meanwhile, Sega’s arcade racing game OutRun is set for a movie adaptation, with Michael Bay and Sydney Sweeney attached .

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

The hard part isn't actually installing the mount properly or even lifting the TV onto the mount, it's actually making sure you have it perfectly level. That's where this practical little doohickey comes in. For a limited time, Amazon is offering a Fanttik D2 Pocket Laser Level for $27.98 when you apply coupon " QWE99JDZ ". Fanttik D2 Pocket Green Laser Level for Under $30

articles.title: PlayStation Blackout Boycott Had 'No Significant Change' on Player Counts or Engagement, Says Analyst
articles.summary: The recent PlayStation blackout boycott reportedly had no "significant" change in player engagement with the platform, according to an analyst.
articles.body:
The recent PlayStation blackout boycott reportedly had no "significant" change in player engagement with the platform, according to an analyst.

Last month, fans organized a boycott against PlayStation for the last week of August as a way of protesting the company's decision to abandon physical media . The boycott asked players to avoid playing their PlayStation, make purchases on the console, or renew any subscriptions to services like PlayStation Plus. Many questioned how effective this would actually be, given the blackout overlapped with the gameplay reveal of GTA 6, which would inevitably drive pre-orders for the game, and the beta for Modern Warfare 4.

As it turns out, it apparently wasn't very impactful. Circana analyst Matt Piscatella noted that the company saw no significant changes in player counts or overall platform engagement on PlayStation during this period. No numbers or hard data were provided on what changes there might've been, but it appears to be negligible. This may come as disappointing news to those who are trying to make their voices heard.

As of right now, it seems unlikely PlayStation is going to back down on its stance regarding physical games, especially as Grand Theft Auto VI likely won't suffer from a lack of a disc . Rumors have suggested that the next Xbox console was planned to have a disc drive prior to the recent "reset." If that's still the plan, Xbox may try to fill the hole left in the physical market with its next console. Microsoft is staying tight-lipped on how it plans to approach physical media with its next-gen console, but it has started implementing features that let players digitize their physical libraries .

Next year will be the final year for PlayStation's support of physical media, meaning games like God of War Laufey and potentially Intergalactic: Heretic Prophet will be the last physical PlayStation exclusives. Maybe something will change, but you probably shouldn't hold your breath.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: This Fantasy Party Game Combines Drinking Rules With D&D-Themed Gameplay
articles.body:
Dungeons & Dragons is one of the most popular tabletop games of all time. And while gameplay for the classic tabletop RPG does always pair well with drinking, it's not specifically designed for it. Thankfully there's an out-of-the-box option that lets you combine drinking and spell-slinging strategy seamlessly. And it's available for pretty cheap right now thanks to a new discount.

Wizards Tavern is officially labeled as a strategy drinking card game for adults. It's based off of the popular Do or Drink card game, but with more D&D and quite a bit less party. Amazon currently has it on sale for $24.99 right now and comes with an extra party game for free.

Wizards Tavern Strategy Drinking Card Game

The way the game works is fairly straightforward. There are a total of 170 cards full of spellcasters and attacks that each player will be able to use. Your health and mana is managed via two drinks you'll need to sip to recover, each of which sits on a specific coaster included. There's also a set of d20 dice colors available representing the eight different wizard types you can choose from.

As a party game , it's meant to be enjoyed with up to eight players but can also be played with as few as two. Presumably the more players you have, the more chaotic the game will get. The rules are also quite simple and easy to understand, making it perfect for folks who aren't tabletop gaming veterans just looking to have a good time and sling some spells.

Amazon Includes a Free Card Game for a Limited Time

In addition to the discount on the game itself, Amazon is offering a promotion right now that tosses in a free card game. On the product page there's a little note that says 'Free bonus item' and if you click to see what it is you'll find a party game called Don't Copy Me . You'll need to add both this item and Wizards Tavern to your cart to get this game for free at checkout.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics — from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .

articles.title: The Popular Budget-Friendly Flashforge Adventurer 5M 3D Printer Drops to Just $135 Shipped
articles.body:
If you're interested in dipping your toes in the world of 3D printing then you can't go wrong with Flashforge's entry level model - the Adventure 5M - as your first 3D printer to start. As part of the AliExpress Fall Sale, you can get it for as low as $136.91 with free shipping after you apply $20 off coupon code " 15USAFF ". The same printer sells for $249 on Amazon . You're buying it from FlashForge's official store on AliExpress. Since it ships for free locally from a warehouse in the United States, delivery usually takes less than a week and there are no extra import fees.

The Adventurer 5M offers great performance at at outstanding budget price. I would say it is the best 3D printer priced below $150. The 5M is easy to setup, produces great 3D prints with minimal fiddling, and offers plenty of add-on mods including a kit that fully encloses the chamber and another that adds a camera .

Flashforge Adventurer 3D Printer Drops to $137

Make sure you're signed into your account to see the shipping options (may need to refresh twice )

FlashForge Adventurer 5M CoreXY 3D Printer

The Adventurer 5M is Flashforge's least expensive CoreXY printer. In fact, it's one of the least expensive CoreXY printers from any well-regarded brand, but with upgrades where they matter. For starters, the Adventurer 5M features a CoreXY structure typically found in pricier models. In a CoreXY printer, only the print head moves while the motors are permanently fixed. Since the motors are generally the heaviest component, this improves print speed and precision.

The open bed has a build volume measuring approximately 8.7" cubed. A closed chamber offers a more controlled environment that eliminates unpredicatable variables like dust or wind and stabilizes temperatures for consistent result. Usually this costs a premium, but FlashForge sells a kit that converts the open bed into a closed chamber for $39.99 . If you want to spend even less and don't care about aesthetics, you can just put a big box over it and call it a day.

The 5M boasts a print speed of up to 600mm/s with 20,000mm/s² acceleration and can print a benchy in 14 minutes. The high-flow 32mm³/s nozzle with 280°C direct extruder can warm up to 200°C in as fast as 35 seconds for consistent filament dispensing. Build quality is solid since all of the structural components are made of metal. The 4.3" color touchscreen control panel is intuitive to use with minimal fiddling and the 5M supports essential features such as auto leveling and vibration compensation. Assembly is quick and easy and you'll be able to print your first object in minutes.

articles.title: Wardogs Players Are Avoiding One of the Game's Factions Because It Has a Stigma of Attracting the Stupidest Players
articles.summary: Wardogs players are avoiding the game's Lonestar faction, as they seemingly attract the worst players and lose the most games.
articles.body:
Wardogs players are avoiding the game's Lonestar faction, as they seemingly attract the worst players and lose the most games.

There are three playable teams in Wardogs: a blue team (Lonestar), a red team (Valkyra), and a green team (Manticore). The different teams don't really have any major gameplay effects, but there is a stigma around Lonestar. For whatever reason, Lonestar has a really difficult time accomplishing much of anything in Wardogs. The team tends to attract the worst and newest players, leading to a major handicap for players on that team. There are a lot of theories as to why this is happening, with one being that it's the first option, so new players pick it by default.

Other teams also fill up extremely quickly because of the stigma, meaning more inexperienced players who don't know any better are sometimes shut out of having other options. One player on Reddit noted that some matches have delayed starts, simply because some players refuse to pick Lonestar, and it leads to the game not starting the match due to a lack of players. You can see one viral clip of Lonestar's antics below to get an idea of the absurdity that some players are experiencing.

I love everything about this clip. Never change Blues 💙 (Thanks to u/pancakerulez for sharing) pic.twitter.com/BvWsRtOd6q — Lossy (@L0SSY) September 14, 2026

I love everything about this clip. Never change Blues 💙 (Thanks to u/pancakerulez for sharing) pic.twitter.com/BvWsRtOd6q

There are instances of Lonestar overcoming the odds and proving the doubters wrong. In my experience, I have never won on Lonestar. All of my wins in Wardogs come from playing with the other two teams. Is that a coincidence? It seems statistically unlikely, but maybe! Hopefully this will iron out as the game's player base becomes more experienced and more well-rounded, but who's to say when that will happen.

Wardogs has been a breakout hit, selling a million copies prior to launch and sitting near the top of Steam's most-played games. The positive word of mouth keeps attracting new players, and that will likely continue over the next few weeks and months, especially as the game already has a slight discount through Fanatical . If you're a console player hoping to get in on the action, you'll have to wait a while. Wardogs is planned to release on Xbox and PS5 in 2028 , so don't expect it anytime soon.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: 2026 Emmy Award Winners: The Full List
articles.body:
That’s another year in the books for the Emmys, this time hosted by Law & Order SVU’s Mariska Hargitay. Widow’s Bay came away as the clear winner of the night, taking six trophies, including closing the night with a win for Best Comedy Series. Kate O’Flynn started the ceremony off strong, winning the comedy supporting actress category for fan-favorite Patricia. Matthew Rhys made history, winning both awards for Actor in a Drama and Comedy Series for The Beast in Me and Widow’s Bay. He’s the first guy to take both trophies in the same year . The Late Show With Stephen Colbert got an awards-show sendoff, taking Best Variety Series (which has gone to Last Week With John Oliver since 2016). Michael J. Fox was honored with the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award for the work he’s done with his foundation on Parkinson’s research. Reba McEntire honored Dolly Parton, singing “Appalachian Memories,” and Macaulay Culkin, Annie Murphy, and Dan Levy gave a funny, touching tribute to Catherine O’Hara tribute to start the In Memoriam segment where Noah Kahan sang “Bridge Over Troubled Water.”

Otherwise, it was a quiet night for basically every other nominated show. Pluribus and The Pitt both came in a distant second to Widow’s Bay trophy count, with two awards each. For Pluribus, Rhea Seehorn won for Actress in a Drama Series (her first Emmy ever) and Vince Gilligan took the prize for Writing in a Drama Series (his first writing Emmy ever). The Pitt nabbed the big Best Drama award, along with Noah Wylie for Best Actor in a Drama. Hacks only took home one Emmy (that went to Jean Smart) for its fifth and final season. A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, Beef, Paradise, The Bear, Abbott Elementary, and other series got completely shut out during the televised ceremony.

articles.summary: A must own set for any LEGO fan and Nintendo gamer.
articles.body:
Here's an opportunity to get one of the best Nintendo-themed LEGO sets at a discount. Walmart is currently offering the LEGO Game Boy 72046 building set for $59.99 with free shipping. That's the same price as every other retailer, however you may be able to get an extra $10 off when you apply coupoon code " SAVE3X ". Your mileage may vary (it might not work for you) but we've confirmed that it is working for a lot of people. Here are the coupon code's details:

Valid on your first three online pickup or delivery orders

Only for new customers (although it actually works for many returning customers)

$10 Off the LEGO Game Boy 72046 Building Kit

The LEGO Game Boy 72046 is a 1:1 replica of the original Nintendo Game Boy handheld that was released way back in 1989. Faithfully rendered details include the two tone gray color scheme, classic control layout with magenta B/A buttons, contrast dial, and speaker grille. All of the text, including the labels and logos, on the handheld are printed blocks. In fact, no stickers are used on the console itself, which is a rarity nowadays.

Speaking of the game cartridges, two are included: Super Mario Land and The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening. Also included are lenticular screens for the respective games. The text elements are printed pieces but the game label itself is a big sticker. This is actually intentional because the original cartridges also used stickers for the labels.

The set is catered towards builders 18+ but it's a fast and fun build. IGN's Seth Macy built this set and it took him about an hour. The target 18+ demographic doesn't come as a surprise, either, since everyone who has fond memories of playing Super Mario Land or Link's Awakening on the Game Boy is probably well older than that. Even at its retail price of $60, this is unquestionably a must-own for any LEGO fan who's into gaming.

articles.title: Valve is still figuring out ‘how and when’ to do Steam Deck 2
articles.summary: Valve designer Pierre-Loup Griffais told IGN that RAM isn’t impacting Steam Deck 2 plans, but those plans don’t sound like they’re soon.
articles.body: Now that Valve has finally launched its entire 2026 hardware lineup — the Steam Controller, the Steam Machine, and today’s Steam Frame — are we any closer to a next-gen Steam Deck handheld? Valve isn’t saying so yet. The company is figuring out “how and when we can deliver something like that,” Valve designer Pierre-Loup Griffais now tells IGN. Valve has been clear for years that 1) a Steam Deck 2 will indeed happen, and 2) it’s not coming until Valve finds the right chip. The original Steam Deck worked because it delivered the right combination of price, performance, and battery life, and Valve has repeatedly said it won’t sacrifice efficiency in the sequel. “We also don’t want more performance to come at a significant cost to power efficiency and battery life,” Griffais told me in 2023, saying he wanted to see a “leap” instead — but suggesting that leap might not be physically possible for another couple of years. Earlier this year, Valve got my hopes up that the wait for a chip was over — when Griffais revealed the team was “hard at work” on the next Steam Deck gaming handheld in an interview with IGN. He wouldn’t say when it might happen. I assumed that was caution, because RAMageddon had already pushed the company to delay and reprice the Steam Machine and Steam Frame headset by then. Today, IGN’s new question was: “Has the current hardware shortage impacted the way Valve is thinking about actually putting a Steam Deck 2 into development?” Griffais’ immediate answer was “Not really.” That could be good news for impatient gamers — or it could mean that the company will wait out RAMageddon before it dares intercept the silicon supply chain again. Valve originally wanted to build a “far more affordable” headset, for instance, but instead it faced brutal RAM negotiations to eventually arrive at a $1,059 pricetag. The real question is: has Valve yet identified the future chip that will appear in the Steam Deck 2? Because the company will work backwards from that chip’s availability to create the hardware it lives within. Intel’s Panther Lake handheld chip in the MSI Claw 8 EX AI Plus is the first I’ve tried that comes close to the kind of “generational leap” that Griffais has been talking about, but Panther Lake handhelds are incredibly expensive, and the Intel chip wasn’t a silver bullet in my tests. But I bet Valve has seen the future of Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm chips, and maybe a future one will do the trick. I hope a Steam Deck 2 will kickstart a new golden age of handheld gaming; I fear it may cost too much for that.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Actor Liam McIntyre Isn't Fazed by Players' Brutal Comments About the Game
articles.summary: Wolverine actor Liam McIntyre has seen what fans are saying about him and Insomniac's latest superhero game, but it's no skin off his nose.
articles.body:
Wolverine actor Liam McIntyre has seen what fans are saying about him and Insomniac's latest superhero game, but it's no skin off his nose.

Marvel’s Wolverine is out in the wild for many players worldwide, and opinions have been strong, to say the least. Discourse around the game has been unavoidable over the last month, with a vocal swath of players taking issue with Insomniac’s art direction, character design, and gameplay segments that were shown off by the media and early reviews.

One of the core topics of the Wolverine debate is actor Liam McIntyre, who plays the game’s titular character. Some fans don’t believe he bears a close enough resemblance to the iconic mutant, while others feel that Insomniac’s face scans and art style didn’t do his visage justice.

McIntyre has been excitedly posting about his role as Wolverine ever since his involvement was first announced, and some players have just now realized that he’s been seeing what they’re saying about him on social media this entire time.

In response to one of these players, McIntyre lightheartedly remarked that he’s seen much worse said about him ever since he started his acting career.

“Ha. Man, my career started with the responsibility of taking over for the incredible Andy Whitfield in Spartacus (RIP to that legend). I've read things you couldn't believe :) I just hope everyone has fun. I'm proud as hell of this game. It's a blast,” he wrote on X.

Ha. Man my career started with the responsibility of taking over for the incredible Andy Whitfield in Spartacus (RIP to that legend). I've read things you couldn't believe :) I just hope everyone has fun. I'm proud as hell of this game. It's a blast. — liam (@Liam_J_McIntyre) September 14, 2026

Ha. Man my career started with the responsibility of taking over for the incredible Andy Whitfield in Spartacus (RIP to that legend). I've read things you couldn't believe :) I just hope everyone has fun. I'm proud as hell of this game. It's a blast.

McIntyre did, indeed, play the historical Spartacus in Starz’s 2010s miniseries of the same name. The late great Andy Whitfield notably played the role of Spartacus in the show’s first season, Blood and Sand, but was diagnosed with stage IV non-Hodgkin lymphoma, a type of cancer that affects the blood, before the second season was filmed.

After his death in 2011, McIntyre was tasked with taking over the role — something that sparked strong reactions from fans at the time, though many now remember his time in the show fondly.

All that is to say, McIntyre is no stranger to vocal opinions from fans in response to taking on the mantle of iconic characters who are known to be played by a certain actor. Wolverine has been portrayed by Hugh Jackman in nearly all modern mainline X-Men films, and McIntyre’s take on the character is a big change for viewers who are used to seeing Jackman on screen — but McIntyre is excited for players to experience his version of the grizzled mutant, come what may.

I don't know what the fates have in store for us tomorrow, but I just want to say thank you to everyone for this once in a lifetime opportunity. Thank you to @MarvelGames and @insomniacgames for trusting me with such a beloved character. I'm so proud. What a journey. pic.twitter.com/xVA3iSbJr6 — liam (@Liam_J_McIntyre) September 10, 2026

I don't know what the fates have in store for us tomorrow, but I just want to say thank you to everyone for this once in a lifetime opportunity. Thank you to @MarvelGames and @insomniacgames for trusting me with such a beloved character. I'm so proud. What a journey. pic.twitter.com/xVA3iSbJr6

Marvel’s Wolverine has been met with mixed reviews from critics; IGN gave the game a six out of 10 , calling it “standard superhero fare” whose “slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion.”

The game is officially coming out tonight for all players, so if you're keen on playing it, tell us what you think about it in the comments below. Does it live up to the hype, or do you think Insomniac's latest offering doesn't break the mold enough to warrant a standout review?

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Anniversary excitement builds among Yorkshire Pokémon fans
articles.summary: Collectors are eagerly awaiting the first release of the 30th anniversary Pokémon trading cards.
articles.body:
For most people, Wednesday will be just another day - the midweek hump at school or work. But not for Pokémon fans.

The Japanese brand has become one of the most recognisable in the world, with its colourful creatures appearing in video games and on shop shelves across the globe.

But perhaps most synonymous with the Pokémon phenomenon is its trading card game, which has been played, bought and sold between collectors for the last three decades.

Wednesday marks the release of Pokémon's 30th anniversary range - a day one collector described as the brand's biggest day "in the last decade, if not more".

Gus Hall, owner of Evolution Games in Halifax, said he expected fans to queue before shops open to get their hands on the first release of the cards.

A long-term Pokémon collector himself, Hall said he was "massively excited" about the anniversary range.

"If you want my personal opinion, I would say this is the biggest release for a good while for Pokémon. Some of the products and the cards they've leaked... are crazy," he said.

Pokémon's popularity has exploded over the years, with some cards originally worth just a few pounds now selling for eye-watering amounts.

Hall said a box that may have been worth £200 in the late 1990s would now sell for about £35,000.

As a child, Hall would spend about £1.99 of his pocket money on a new Pokémon card. His parents would "go ballistic" at him for what they believed was a waste of money.

He said: "They'd say to me: 'Why are you wasting your money on these types of things?'… Now I get the exact same from parents who come into my store and say to their children: 'Why are you wasting your money on these [cards]?'… But, you know, look who's laughing now!"

But what has made these cards so popular - and so valuable?

"Pokémon is different to other things in society these days - there's nothing electronic in trading cards," Hall said.

"Parents quite like it because it's healthy; it creates friendships and trading and gaming, and incorporates all these wonderful things that aren't detrimental to a child or young person's mind."

Hall said the satisfaction of collecting a set and "chasing certain cards" in that set was a huge part of the enjoyment, and described the moment of pulling the desired card as "euphoric".

Phoebe Watson, an employee at Evolution Games, has been collecting Pokémon cards for the last 20 years.

She said she was "super excited" for the first release of the anniversary range and was hoping to secure some of the cards, which feature some of her favourite Pokémons.

But Watson is realistic - she expects the first release to sell out quickly.

"It is going to be big. We get collectors in every single day, multiple times a day, and I've had hundreds of people ask me: 'When is the set dropping? Do you know how much you're getting?'."

Drew Emerson, one of Europe's top Pokémon players, told BBC Radio Sheffield he had "travelled all over the world" playing the trading card game.

Emerson said it was going to be "very, very difficult" to secure the anniversary cards on first release, but added the collection was "very, very exciting".

Pokémon is reprinting old, rare cards, Emerson said, and he was "most looking forward" to the release of a Crystal Lugia card.

Pokémon, originally called Pocket Monsters, began as a game released for the Nintendo Gameboy in Japan in 1996.

Millions of copies were sold worldwide and the name was eventually shortened to Pokémon.

Following the success of the first games, a company called Media Factory released the Pokémon Trading Card Game in October that year. Like the game, the cards exploded in popularity.

Since then, more than 85 billion cards have been produced, a world championship tournament established, and an ultra-rare card sold for $16.5m (£12m).

Lee Glen, owner of trading card stores Rocket's Hideout in York and Selby, said Pokémon cards had "exploded" in the last five years, which he largely attributed to the hobby being "multi-generational".

"I got back into collecting five years ago with my son. It was something nostalgic that I used to do, and then got back into it with my son… You have sons, daughters, mums, everyone - and they can do it together," Glen said.

He said Pokémon was "constantly reinventing" products, and was "really good at bringing people back in".

Glen's York store is usually closed on Wednesdays, but it will open specially for the first release, when Glen too expects customers to flock to York to get their hands on the stock.

Among those hoping to secure some anniversary cards is 21-year-old Grace Orton, who said she was willing to queue up to get her hands on them.

"I'll definitely be trying at some point to get some. I know it'll be really difficult if I'm not [at a shop] immediately", Orton said.

Despite only starting her Pokémon card collection three years ago, Orton said she was "looking to spend quite a bit of money, unfortunately" on the anniversary range.

She said: "It's such a big, sought-after set. A lot of the artwork is really nice; I really want some of it for my personal collection."

Another Pokémon fanatic, Ash Mehr, said he started collecting the cards between 20 and 30 years ago.

After a brief hiatus, Mehr began his collection once again after his son took an interest in Pokémon.

He said: "I feel like I'm sort of dragging my son to these events to try and get the cards, but really it's a little bit of a guilty pleasure of mine! But hopefully, we'll get a good haul and get some good pulls [from the anniversary range]".

There is a huge sense of nostalgia surrounding the 30th anniversary of Pokémon cards, Mehr said, adding: "It takes me back to being a kid, really, something I don't get to enjoy now as much in my early 40s."

But with high-value products comes risk - and Glen has warned of Pokémon fans being scammed around the release of the anniversary range.

He encouraged people to buy the cards from national and independent retailers, and avoid "secondary markets", which may be used to re-sell the cards at "two or three times" the price.

He said: "Just research and know what to spend.

"If it looks too cheap, chances are it is… because of the desirability of a product, people will always try and copy [them]. Do your homework."

Listen to highlights from North Yorkshire on BBC Sounds , catch up with the latest episode of Look North .

Pokémon star catches 'em all at World Championships

Who were the winners at Pokémon's biggest battle?

images.caption: Pokémon collector Grace Orton hopes to secure some anniversary cards

articles.title: James Bond Game 007 First Light Delayed Until 2027 on Nintendo Switch 2
articles.summary: James Bond game 007 First Light has been delayed yet again on Nintendo Switch 2, and will now arrive in March 2027.
articles.body:
James Bond game 007 First Light has been delayed yet again on Nintendo Switch 2, and will now arrive in March 2027.

007 First Light was originally expected to land back in May this year on all platforms simultaneously. In April, however, Hitman developer IO Interactive announced a last-minute delay for the Switch 2 version, and stated it would now arrive this fall.

Well, that date has also now fallen through, with a further, lengthy delay until its new release window next March. In a statement posted to social media this morning, IO said it would provide an exact release date nearer the time.

"We know many of you have been looking forward to experiencing Bond's reimagined origin story on Nintendo Switch 2, and we greatly appreciate your enthusiasm," IO wrote. "To ensure we deliver the quality of experience players expect, we have made the decision to delay the release to March 2027, with the exact date to be communicated later. This additional time will go toward polishing the Nintendo Switch 2 performance of the game.

"We were thrilled by the positive feedback on 007 First Light at Gamescom, and it's a great sign of the progress being made across the whole game as we head toward launch," IO continued. "The same demo will be playable at Tokyo Game Show this week, so please join us there if you would like a hands-on experience.

"We will share further updates as soon as we are ready. Thank you for your patience, understanding, and continued support."

For the majority of fans, popping over to Tokyo this week to try the Switch 2 version will likely seem a little excessive. And yet again, it's unclear why the game's Switch 2 version has been delayed relatively close to its expected release. If the game isn't struggling technically, is this a decision made to launch the title when the console has a larger userbase? Is there are fear of arriving too close to GTA 6? And what are the trade-offs to waiting even longer, as hype for the game dies down? IO has not said.

IO announced the news today alongside a fresh update for First Light on PC, which adds path tracing and DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support, in a bid for even more impressive lighting, shadows and reflections. Other upcoming additions include a new story DLC centered around Bawama, the pirate king warlord played by Lenny Kravitz , plus additional TacSim challenges, a fresh gadget, New Game+, and a photo mode.

"Demonstrably obsessed with bringing the Bond fantasy to life in a way no one has ever managed before, 007 First Light is the best Bond game I’ve ever played," IGN wrote in our 007 First Light review , awarding the game a 009/10.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: US Confirms for the First Time It Has Deployed a Space Weapon in Earth's Orbit
articles.summary: It sounds like something ripped straight out of a science fiction war movie, but it is now a reality: the U.S. has, for the first time, confirmed it has deployed a space weapon in Earth’s orbit.
articles.body:
It sounds like something ripped straight out of a science fiction war movie, but it is now a reality: the U.S. has, for the first time, confirmed it has deployed a space weapon in Earth’s orbit.

Confirmation comes from Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink, who was speaking at the Air, Space and Cyber Conference on Monday. He insisted the space weapon was about protecting U.S. forces.

“Today we continue to ensure we remain ready to meet the challenges of evolving threats wherever they exist. This is why the United States now has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the joint force against hostile adversary action.”

“It is critically important that we maintain our dominance not only in the air but in space, and so we’ve had to take steps to make sure that when we’re threatened, we can take care of that,” Meink continued.

Meink refused to explain what the weapon was capable of doing, or when it was put in orbit. Nor do we know if the weapon has already been used.

U.S. officials have hinted at having offensive and defensive space capabilities for some time now, but this is the first time someone has gone on the record to confirm it. There’s a great deal of speculation about what the weapon may be. Some think it could be a kinetic weapon that could actually crash into something, perhaps a satellite, and blow it up. Others think it’s more likely a jammer or a directed energy weapon, one that wouldn’t cause damaging space debris.

The Trump administration has in the past talked about space weapons forming part of the U.S.’s anti-air ‘Golden dome’ defence system, having set up the Space Force in 2019 to work on space capabilities. A spokesperson for the U.S. Space Force told the BBC : "Space control encapsulates the mission areas required to contest and control the space domain — employing kinetic and non-kinetic means to affect adversary capabilities through disruption, degradation and even destruction, if necessary. These capabilities can be employed for offensive and defensive purposes at the direction of combatant commands."

There are some who believe the next war could start in space, with an adversary perhaps taking out a satellite in an action that would disable communications on earth. This could in turn have a significant impact on a country’s military operations. Space weapons could also theoretically be used to knock long-range missiles that enter orbit out of their trajectory.

The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bans weapons of mass destruction in orbit, but it does not prohibit the use of conventional weapons in space or the use of ground-based weapons against assets in space.

Last year, Donald Trump signed an executive order calling U.S superiority in space “a measure of national vision and willpower.” Speaking at the conference, Meink said a U.S. space-based interceptor program had moved “from initial contract to flight-ready hardware in less than one year.”

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Is Eternal Darkness Getting a Remaster? Nightdive Studios Raises Hopes That the GameCube Classic Will Return
articles.summary: Hopes of an Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem remaster have been raised by an intriguing comment from Nightdive Studios.
articles.body:
Hopes of an Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem remaster have been raised by an intriguing comment from Nightdive Studios.

The talented team at Nightdive are port and remaster specialists who have previously dusted off dozens of classic video games for re-release. These include various titles in the System Shock, Quake, Doom and Turok franchises, plus Heretic + Hexen and Thief: The Dark Project.

Now owned by Atari, Nightdive has found an audience with its enhanced ports, which typically receive a lick of visual paint while remaining true to their original forms. And, of course, Nightdive does this in collaboration with the games' original development studio where possible.

Could long-lost classic Eternal Darkness be next? Responding to a fan request via social media yesterday on the 25th anniversary of the GameCube , Nightdive CEO Stephen Kick had this to say: "Eternal Darkness is one of my all-time favorites and it deserves the treatment I know Nightdive Studios is capable of," Kick wrote . "Keep your eye on our Deep Dives..."

Here, Kick is referring to the studio's lengthy videos it releases via YouTube, discussing the various projects it has taken on. Surely this is a suggestion that Eternal Darkness will be next?

Perhaps, though, it's worth remaining cautious until anything is officially announced. Nightdive has attempted to work on Nintendo-published games before, but has never quite got close enough. In 2022, Kick commented that the Mario maker "always get[s] gun shy working with third-party developers," despite discussions to work on an array of its games. One of these was a remaster of the N64 classic Goldeneye 007 that Nintendo ultimately decided against — only to drop the original on Nintendo Switch Online instead. Still, Kick has long maintained that Eternal Darkness is his favorite Nintendo game he'd like Nightdive to work on.

Developed by Silicon Knights, the survival horror adventure launched for the GameCube back in 2002 and became a cult classic for Nintendo fans who were impressed (and suitably freaked out) by the game's creepy sanity mechanics, which Nintendo itself locked down with a patent.

Eternal Darkness sees players controlling an array of characters throughout history, each of which can descend into madness if you're not careful. The psychological effects of this are then experienced by the player, from subtle noises and skewed camera angles, to visual effects such as bleeding walls or moving statues. At its most extreme, the game begins breaking the fourth wall, appearing to reset progress or mute players' TVs. It's enough to make you want to go mad on purpose, just to see how wacky the game gets.

But despite strong reviews, Eternal Darkness sold relatively poorly. Plans for a sequel were discussed for years, though various issues within Silicon Knights hampered progress, and a later push for a spiritual successor via a crowdfunding campaign also fell by the wayside. Silicon Knights ultimately shut down in 2014, while Nintendo's patent for the game's sanity system is now believed to have lapsed.

Is it finally time to descend into madness once more? Here's hoping.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Buffy the Vampire Slayer Reboot Cancellation Means Fans Will Never Discover if Buffy and Angel Ended Up Together, Sarah Michelle Gellar Jokes
articles.summary: Hulu's shock cancellation of its Buffy the Vampire Slayer reboot means that fans will never discover if Buffy and Angel ultimately ended up together.
articles.body:
Hulu's shock cancellation of its Buffy the Vampire Slayer reboot means that fans will never discover if Buffy and Angel ultimately ended up together.

That's according to the Slayer herself, Sarah Michelle Gellar, who reunited with Angel actor David Boreanaz last night at the Emmy Awards. As the pair took the stage together to present a prize, the duo chatted about their characters and also paid tribute to their trio of co-stars who have passed away over the last couple of years.

"You know Sarah, I always thought Buffy and Angel would end up together," Boreanaz said at one point.

"Well, I guess we won't find out," Gellar responded, in a pointed comment that drew laughs from the room, as the audience realized this was a not-so-veiled reference to Hulu's series being scrapped .

The Best Buffy the Vampire Slayer Episodes

Gellar was heavily involved in plans for a soft reboot of the cult series, now updated for the modern day in a fresh version of Sunnydale, and with a new young Slayer as its lead. Gellar herself would have appeared as a recurring character, and other Buffy alumni would have made guest appearances (Spike actor James Marsters has said he expected to pop up at some point, though likely not until the show's second season).

Could Angel have appeared too at some point, in order to wrap up the series' infamous love triangle? Or would Spike and Buffy fans continue to think their true pairing had a chance? As Gellar says, it seems we won't find out.

Sarah Michelle Gellar & David Boreanaz have a Buffy reunion and give nod to late cast members Anthony Head, Michelle Trachtenberg and Nicholas Brendon #Emmys pic.twitter.com/zpLcscG3NR — Deadline (@DEADLINE) September 15, 2026

Sarah Michelle Gellar & David Boreanaz have a Buffy reunion and give nod to late cast members Anthony Head, Michelle Trachtenberg and Nicholas Brendon #Emmys pic.twitter.com/zpLcscG3NR

Various reports have suggested that the reboot's original pilot script — the one that has now partially leaked — featured only a brief appearance by Gellar at the end of the episode. While her character was clearly being set up to appear in an expanded role in later stories (and it perhaps makes sense that the pilot focused on establishing its new cast) Hulu apparently balked at Buffy herself only getting a single line, and asked for a do-over with far more screemtime for Gellar .

Gellar previously pinned the reboot's cancellation squarely on a single executive who she claimed had boasted about never being a Buffy fan . Reports have suggested Hulu remains keen to try another attempt at a Buffy reboot in a few years, though it currently seems unlikely for Gellar to be convinced again — meaning Angel and Buffy fans will just have to wonder what could have been.

"Before we move on to the award, David and I would like to acknowledge that it has been a tough two years for our beloved cast and crew," Gellar concluded, in a clear nod to the recent passing of Anthony Stewart Head (Giles), Nicholas Brendon (Xander) and Michelle Trachtenberg (Dawn). "We feel very lucky to have known and worked with such amazing people."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Wardogs Sells 2 Million Copies in 5 Days as Early Access Shooter Blows Up on Steam
articles.summary: Wardogs’ incredible success has seen it sell 2 million copies after just five days of release.
articles.body:
Wardogs ’ incredible success has seen it sell 2 million copies after just five days of release.

Bulkhead’s tactical first-person shooter released in early access form on Steam on September 10 and was an instant hit, reaching a peak of 428,666 concurrent players and becoming one of the most-played games on Valve’s platform. It sold 1 million copies on day one, and 1.25 million by day two.

“Thank you all. Beyond humbled,” Bulkhead said in a post on social media . “We made a game we wanted to play with friends. Watching you play it with yours has been the best.”

User reviews are now ‘Very Positive’ after initial complaints around launch problems. That appears to be done and dusted now, with players getting on with the game and having fun. A number of gameplay clips showing Wardogs shenanigans have gone viral ( players are even avoiding Wardogs’ Lonestar faction over a perception that they seemingly attract the worst players and lose the most games ).

Bulkhead has said it expects Wardogs to remain in early access for 1-2 years, with a console version planned for 2028. “We are adamant that we do not want to be in Early Access for a long time,” its Steam page reads.

“That time is planned for expanding content, improving systems, refining balance, and responding to player feedback. The exact duration may change depending on how development and community feedback evolves.”

“The full version of Wardogs, whenever it comes out, will be “broader and more polished” than the early access release, Bulkhead has said. Because of this, expect the price of the game to go up when the full release comes out “to reflect the more complete experience.”

“Early access players benefit from getting in at a lower price and helping shape the game as it develops,” Bulkhead has said.

As for the expansion of the game, expect more maps, weapons, vehicles, and gameplay variety. The priority now is building “deeper reasons to play beyond individual matches.”

“We plan to develop more in depth progression systems, a stronger seasonal meta game, and additional systems that reward players for the time and impact they bring to a match, whether through combat, support, or logistics,” Bulkhead said.

“Alongside this, we plan broader gameplay additions such as new vehicle types including fighter jets, expanded weapon categories, additional objective variations, and continued improvements to the core Wardogs experience.

“Throughout Early Access and beyond, our ongoing priority will always be improving balance, performance, and stability.”

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.
